fields.ic_name: ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) — ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C)
fields.power_intent_present: partial — ADIv5 specifies CSYSPWRUPREQ / CDBGPWRUPREQ / CDBGRSTREQ control bits in CTRL/STAT that explicitly drive SoC-level power and reset state, but does not formally define UPF / CPF power-domain partitioning. The DAP itself typically resides in an always-on debug-power domain so it can be reached when functional logic is powered down.

low_power_modes_summary.CSYSPWRUPREQ_ACK_handshake: Host writes CTRL/STAT.CSYSPWRUPREQ=1 to request the SoC bring up the system power domain; host reads CTRL/STAT and waits for CSYSPWRUPACK=1. Used to wake the SoC from deep sleep so the host can access functional memory.
low_power_modes_summary.CDBGPWRUPREQ_ACK_handshake: Host writes CTRL/STAT.CDBGPWRUPREQ=1 to request the SoC bring up the debug power domain (where the CPU debug-control registers live); host waits for CDBGPWRUPACK=1. Without this, accessing DHCSR / DCRSR / DCRDR returns FAULT.
low_power_modes_summary.CDBGRSTREQ_ACK_handshake: Host writes CTRL/STAT.CDBGRSTREQ=1 to request a debug-power reset of the SoC; host waits for CDBGRSTACK=1; clears the request bit.
low_power_modes_summary.SWCLK_stopped_in_idle: When the host stops SWCLK between transactions, the SW-DP wire-level FSM holds its current Idle state. Dynamic current drops to leakage.
low_power_modes_summary.DAP_always_on_partitioning: Typical SoCs place the SW-DP wire-level FSM + DP register set in an always-on debug-power domain so the host can probe the SoC even when the system power domain is gated off; the AP layer + MEM-AP bus interface power up only when CDBGPWRUPREQ + CSYSPWRUPREQ are asserted.

swd_in_deep_sleep_use_case: Cortex-M MCUs typically enter WFI/WFE / standby / deep-sleep with the CPU clock gated. The SW-DP can remain alive in the always-on domain.
Host probe asserts CDBGPWRUPREQ + CSYSPWRUPREQ to wake the debug + system power domains so it can access the CPU's DHCSR + memory.
After debug session ends, host clears the request bits so the SoC can re-enter deep sleep.
Some MCUs (e.g. NXP K-series, ST L-series) specifically advertise 'debug-during-stop-mode' capability — SWD remains responsive in STOP/STANDBY low-power modes for non-intrusive debug.
wake_on_debug: ARM CoreSight DAP supports 'wake-on-debug': the SW-DP detects host activity on SWCLK and wakes the SoC's debug power domain.
Implementation is vendor-specific but the protocol mechanism is the CDBGPWRUPREQ handshake.
Used heavily in deep-sleep MCU debug scenarios.
isolation_clamps_during_power_gate: When the system power domain is gated off but the debug power domain is alive, isolation clamps are required between the MEM-AP and the gated system bus. Host accesses return FAULT (STICKYERR) until the system domain is brought back up.
These isolation cells are implementation-specific and reside on the AP-to-system-bus boundary; ADIv5 does not standardize them but assumes they are present.

ctrl_stat_power_bits_summary.bit_28: CDBGPWRUPREQ — host request to power up the debug domain.
ctrl_stat_power_bits_summary.bit_29: CDBGPWRUPACK — target acknowledge of debug power up.
ctrl_stat_power_bits_summary.bit_30: CSYSPWRUPREQ — host request to power up the system domain.
ctrl_stat_power_bits_summary.bit_31: CSYSPWRUPACK — target acknowledge of system power up.
ctrl_stat_power_bits_summary.bit_26: CDBGRSTREQ — host request a debug-domain reset.
ctrl_stat_power_bits_summary.bit_27: CDBGRSTACK — target acknowledge of debug reset.

fields.notes: ADIv5 explicitly provides protocol-level handshakes for debug + system power-up so that the host can wake a sleeping SoC and reach the CPU's debug-control registers. This is fundamentally more sophisticated than IEEE 1149.1 JTAG, which has no concept of power-up handshakes. In practice, MCU vendors implement the always-on debug-power domain by routing the DP + SW-DP wire-level FSM to an always-on power rail (often the SoC's VBAT or VDD-IO domain) and gating the AP layer to the main VDD-CORE domain. Modern Cortex-M0+/M23/M33 parts typically advertise < 100 µA standby current including an always-on SW-DP. CMSIS-DAP probes always issue CSYSPWRUPREQ + CDBGPWRUPREQ + STKERRCLR + STKCMPCLR + WDERRCLR + ORUNERRCLR as part of their connect-sequence to ensure the SoC is awake and clean before any AP transaction.
